# NH Pre-V10 History vs V10 Feature Recovery Ledger v0.1

Audit date: 2026-09-24. Repository: `nesgeva/NH-GOVERNANCE`. Branch: `main`. Requested commit: `3aa08a2`; resolved and verified full commit: `3aa08a29f2d260c42502255001549cc11df24048`. Complete Git tree: `d2572a73def135cc9bac5e24664faf4a9823249a`; tree response reported `truncated=false`.

## Scope and governing authority

Ness's adoption of `01_AUTHORITATIVE/NH_MASTER-20_CORRECTED_v10.md` on 2026-06-29 governs this audit. The order is Master V10 → `01_AUTHORITATIVE/NH_DECISION_DEFAULTS-S19_v2_2.md` → `01_AUTHORITATIVE/cursorrules` → `01_AUTHORITATIVE/NH_PROJECT_COMPANION_GOVERNANCE_AND_ARCHIVE_v1.md`. The working Map is subordinate. Decision Index v0_11 supplies navigation and NHD identifiers, not authority. An accepted package is treated as accepted only within its recorded acceptance scope. Folder placement does not create acceptance.

All archive documents are historical under the task's cutoff. Their old references to Master-19 v7_1 as authoritative, and V10's retained candidate header, do not override Ness's adoption. Historical material reproduced inside Companion Part V is preservation evidence, not an operative reinstatement of that material. No implementation, machine state, present-day price, or model performance was independently tested. No repository file was edited. No governance choice is made or proposed here.

The report contains **1233 classified item rows** after merging overlapping checklist entries. These are documentary items, not a count of distinct product features: a named historical script, a schema contract, a control rule, and a broad capability have different granularity. A feature can remain while one of its details or named tools is missing. The item column and explanation bound each classification.

| Classification | Rows |
|---|---:|
| DROPPED | 87 |
| CONTRADICTED | 20 |
| COMPRESSED | 51 |
| SUPERSEDED | 130 |
| CARRIED | 945 |
| NOT-ASSESSED | 0 |

**Reading method.** Every unpacked historical file was returned whole through the GitHub connector, checked against pinned Git blob identity and byte length, then fully covered as text. Long repeated versions were not each independently reread end to end: all changed or unique passages were directly read and every reused line/span was matched exactly to already read source text. Headings and changed passages were read in context. Master V10 received a complete continuous team read. A search result alone never counted as a full source read. Local display truncations were repaired with bounded rereads; no truncated connector file was treated as complete. Scripts, HTML and SVG were inspected as text, not executed or visually evaluated.

**Absence scope.** DROPPED means no operative counterpart was located in the complete retrieved current corpus: folders 01, 02, 03, 04, 05 active/inactive, 06, and continuation context (144 files). Checks used names, wording variants, and related governing sections. Unaccepted proposals and historical quotations do not establish current carryover. Relevant accepted-package sections were read; the audit does not claim an independent full semantic read of every current supporting file. The exact limit is listed below. COMPRESSED means the parent feature survives but the quoted specific requirement/detail was not retained. CONTRADICTED records different statements without resolving them. SUPERSEDED records an explicit settled replacement with an NHD reference; that decision is not reopened. CARRIED does not certify historical built-status claims or imply all adjacent details survived.

### Metadata discrepancies and coverage gaps

1. README “What is in this folder” says “Sixty-plus files across three batches”; the folder and INDEX have 58 recovered bodies.
2. INDEX “Unrecoverable historical body (recorded, not substituted)” retains “not resident anywhere” for the earlier Meaning Engine body. The later recovered row identifies it, with the same historical SHA-256. It is present; the earlier wording is stale.
3. INDEX “Fingerprints of the three still-missing candidate files” retains historical missing wording. Later batch rows and the closing note satisfy that table. All three bodies are present.
4. README/INDEX describe a complete Master-20 lineage with every change/provenance and no-loss report. The folder has Master-20 v8 and its change/provenance report, but no v8 no-loss report. None is presumed to have existed.
5. INDEX says the ZIP “was not available when this archive was produced”; a later row and the pinned tree show it present. The binary was deliberately skipped.

The archive checksum manifest was read completely. All **151 downloaded files named in SHA256SUMS.txt** match their listed SHA-256 values. The two excluded album/ZIP values were not independently verified. SHA256SUMS.txt does not hash itself. These are integrity checks, not authority or completeness endorsements.

**Inventory batch fully read:** `README.md`, `INDEX.md`; complete tree metadata inspected. **Not yet read at that boundary:** all 148 files in the table, the root feature catalogue and `SHA256SUMS.txt`. The album and ZIP were excluded by instruction.

## Stage 2 — feature-recovery ledger

### Worked example verified first

Master-8, Master-9, Master-9_2 and Master-9_4, each §9A “IMAGE INGEST — THE FIRST WORKED FRONT-DOOR EXAMPLE,” contain:

> Best done with an **object-detection / segmentation model** (YOLO / Segment-Anything class — e.g. via `osam`/Ollama locally), NOT a narrating vision-language model.

They also name PaddleOCR-VL and SmolVLM. Master-10, its `NH_MASTER-10__1_.md` duplicate, and Master-11 retain shorter detector-versus-narrator guidance and those two names; Master-11_1 thins further. Current V10 §9A says:

> Metadata → plain-description → context-meaning → Ness confirms. Precondition for WhatsApp media (§12).

**DROPPED:** the model-choice guidance, named candidates and specific osam/Ollama image route. **CARRIED:** the four-stage image-ingest outline. **COMPRESSED:** its label/box/confidence output contract, vocabulary limitation and handoff details. Ollama remains named for the language-model role elsewhere; its whole existence is not reported dropped. The ledger separates these items.

#### CONTRADICTED

| FR-0088 — June29 async queue claim uses O_CREAT/O_EXCL versus an OS-held lock | CONTRADICTED | 98_HISTORICAL_SOURCES_PRE_V10/sources_recovered/NH_SESSION_REFERENCE_June29_2026.md §4A Async reading queue and reading-pass instruction log<br>Quote: - Queue-claim mechanism uses a lock file (`O_CREAT\|O_EXCL`) with `job_claimed` and `claim_expired` events to prevent duplicate processing. | 01_AUTHORITATIVE/NH_MASTER-20_CORRECTED_v10.md §7G-A / JOB-PROCESSING LOCK AND CLAIM MECHANISM / Stale-claim takeover after crash; 05_ACTIVE_CANDIDATE/NH_DECISION_INDEX_PROPOSAL_v0_11_CANDIDATE.md NHD-M7G<br>Quote: **Stale-claim takeover after crash.** On startup, if `.nh_queue.lock` exists: the recovery worker attempts to acquire the OS-level exclusive lock on the existing file (non-blocking). If acquisition succeeds: the previous holder crashed (the OS released the lock automatically on process exit). The recovery worker reads the stale claim metadata, overwrites it with new claim metadata (`claim_id`, `worker_id`, `locked_at`, `expires_at`), appends a `claim_expired` event, appends a new `job_claimed` event, and begins recovery. If acquisition fails: another process is still running and holds the lock; no takeover occurs; the recovery worker exits. No lock file is deleted and re-created; no `O_CREAT \| O_EXCL` is used on `.nh_queue.lock`. | The session summary assigns exclusivity to O_CREAT\|O_EXCL. Current V10 instead requires an OS-level exclusive lock held continuously for the claim, and explicitly forbids O_CREAT \| O_EXCL on .nh_queue.lock. job_claimed and claim_expired events survive, but they do not preserve the old locking mechanism. This reports the wording difference and does not select a mechanism or reopen the governing rule. |

| FR-0112 — Universal operational-record ten-part content contract | COMPRESSED | 98_HISTORICAL_SOURCES_PRE_V10/sources_recovered/NH_FINAL_MASTER_RECOVERY_STAGE_3A_SUPPLEMENTAL_CANDIDATE_INTAKE_v1_1.md §5 / F4; 98_HISTORICAL_SOURCES_PRE_V10/sources_recovered/NH_MASTER-19_CORRECTED_v8(1).md §0B WHAT EVERY RECORD MUST CONTAIN<br>Quote: A record is not complete unless it preserves:<br>— what component or process produced it;<br>— what the operation, event, or state was;<br>— when it occurred;<br>— what inputs were supplied and from where;<br>— what was decided, produced, or output;<br>— what was omitted, rejected, failed, or left unknown, and why;<br>— what alternatives existed and were not chosen;<br>— what uncertainty remained;<br>— what connections to other records are established or proposed;<br>— what it was used for, when, by which component, and with what result — every time it is used. | 01_AUTHORITATIVE/NH_MASTER-20_CORRECTED_v10.md §0B FULL-TRANSPARENCY AND LIVING-RECORD LAW  [DESIGNED — foundational operating rule]<br>Quote: **Operational recordkeeping is mandatory for every component.** Every component designed or built must include explicit, mandatory recordkeeping for its own internal operations — not only for what it stores externally, but for every internal retrieval it makes, every context choice, every acceptance or rejection, every omission, every failure, every use of a prior record, and every non-use of a candidate record. | FR-0114 — Recursive self-examination trigger enumeration and no maximum depth | COMPRESSED | 98_HISTORICAL_SOURCES_PRE_V10/sources_recovered/NH_FINAL_MASTER_RECOVERY_STAGE_3A_SUPPLEMENTAL_CANDIDATE_INTAKE_v1_1.md §5 / F6; 98_HISTORICAL_SOURCES_PRE_V10/sources_recovered/NH_MASTER-19_CORRECTED_v8(1).md §0B RECURSIVE SELF-EXAMINATION<br>Quote: Recursive examination is triggered — not automatic. A recursive examination occurs when triggered by: a relevance signal in the current processing context; a system purpose that genuinely requires it; a design rule that specifies it; a detected inconsistency or anomaly; a question from Ness; or another explicitly authorized trigger. When a trigger occurs, the examination runs as deep as the trigger genuinely requires. There is no fixed maximum depth when deeper examination serves a real purpose. There is also no uncontrolled automatic recursion in the absence of a trigger.<br><br>Every recursive examination that is triggered and actually performed must be recorded the same way as any other operation: what triggered it, what records were examined, what was found, what was done with the result, what remained uncertain, and what connections were established. | 01_AUTHORITATIVE/NH_MASTER-20_CORRECTED_v10.md §0B FULL-TRANSPARENCY AND LIVING-RECORD LAW  [DESIGNED — foundational operating rule]<br>Quote: **The operational record is part of N.H's living memory.** It is subject to internal retrieval, connection-building, reading, interpretation, and triggered recursive self-examination — not a passive audit trail. Hiding, restricting, or removing material from visible output does not remove its internal usability or its presence in operational records unless Ness separately instructs that. | V10 keeps triggered recursive examination and one-real-operation/one-log. | FR-0575 — June29 — job_claimed and claim_expired queue events | CARRIED | 98_HISTORICAL_SOURCES_PRE_V10/sources_recovered/NH_SESSION_REFERENCE_June29_2026.md §4A<br>Quote: `job_claimed` and `claim_expired` events | 01_AUTHORITATIVE/NH_MASTER-20_CORRECTED_v10.md §7G MEANING ENGINE INTERIOR  [CONCEPTUALLY DESIGNED, NOT BUILT]<br>Quote: **Stale-claim takeover after crash.** On startup, if `.nh_queue.lock` exists: the recovery worker attempts to acquire the OS-level exclusive lock on the existing file (non-blocking). If acquisition succeeds: the previous holder crashed (the OS released the lock automatically on process exit). The recovery worker reads the stale claim metadata, overwrites it with new claim metadata (`claim_id`, `worker_id`, `locked_at`, `expires_at`), appends a `claim_expired` event, appends a new `job_claimed` event, and begins recovery. If acquisition fails: another process is still running and holds the lock; no takeover occurs; the recovery worker exits. No lock file is deleted and re-created; no `O_CREAT \| O_EXCL` is used on `.nh_queue.lock`. | The named claim-acquisition and stale-claim events are retained. The historical O_CREAT/O_EXCL locking mechanism is a separate CONTRADICTED finding in recovery_final_additions.json; this CARRIED row covers the events only. |

| FR-1163 — Universal Filter R6 — MEMORY ONLY ADDS. IT NEVER EDITS. (THE KEYSTONE) | CARRIED | 98_HISTORICAL_SOURCES_PRE_V10/sources/NH_Universal_Filter_RULES.md — RULE 6 — MEMORY ONLY ADDS. It must never lie about its own past, because it never deletes its past.<br><br>**FORBIDDEN:** editing, overwriting, correcting-in-place, deleting, merging-away, or "cleaning up" any stored reading. ## Stage 3 — last-mile drift

**Direct answer to the no-loss question.** Across the completely compared corrected v1→v2→…→v9 transitions, this audit did not establish an unreported next-version omission contradicting a preceding report’s preservation claim. LM-R01–LM-R05 below concern contradictions or unfinished reconciliation already present in the version being certified and then corrected; they do not establish a new loss in the next version. For v9→V10, the old limitation on entry into `promotion_failed` is absent, within the five expressly reported changed regions. That replacement is established; its intendedness is not. The comparison neither proves nor disproves the reports’ intent-qualified “unintended loss 0” claims.

Pinned source: `3aa08a29f2d260c42502255001549cc11df24048`. This audit compares history with the adopted V10; no historical authority claim is made current.

**Result.** All complete bytes were compared for initial Master-20 → corrected v1 → v2 → v3 → v4 → v5 → v6 → v7 → v8 → v9 → adopted V10. Every changed old-side and new-side passage was read with surrounding context. The v9→V10 change report correctly identifies five changed regions, with no unrelated deletion: identity and TSC §§17, 20, 23, 27. One old constraint is no longer retained: v9’s limitation of entry into `promotion_failed` to non-retryable/exhausted failures. The remaining changed lifecycle passages preserve and expand the earlier behavior. Their exact old text appears below. No conclusion about intendedness is made.

**Limits of no-loss reports.** A report saying “unintended loss 0” is not independent proof of preserved meaning. The lineage contains documented replacements, and some historical verification claims overstate the reconciliation then achieved. The following report findings do not allege an undocumented feature removal and do not challenge V10 adoption.

## Earlier recovery-closure claim



This is provenance drift, separate from any judgment about Ness's adoptions.

`98_HISTORICAL_SOURCES_PRE_V10/sources_recovered/NH_FINAL_MASTER_RECOVERY_STAGE_3B_CANDIDATE_IMPACT_AND_CLOSURE_v1.md`, opening, says: “Stages 1, 2, and 3A already performed the historical feature recovery.” The same opening says “The full historical inventory was **not** rebuilt.” Its declared historical-preservation work was a phrase scan for feature-level adoption evidence.

The earlier records do not establish the claimed completed full historical comparison:

- `98_HISTORICAL_SOURCES_PRE_V10/sources_recovered/NH_FINAL_MASTER_RECOVERY_STAGE_1_LINEAGE_AND_AUDIT_PLAN_v1_2.md` §9 **STATE AFTER STAGE 1** says “No candidate adopted. No conflict resolved. No feature compared. No patch proposed.”
- `98_HISTORICAL_SOURCES_PRE_V10/sources_recovered/NH_FINAL_MASTER_RECOVERY_STAGE_2_CHRONOLOGY_VERIFICATION_v1_1.md` §8/summary says “No feature compared, no conflict resolved, no design judged, nothing integrated or patched”; §9.1 says historical design bodies were not read in full for chronology.
- `98_HISTORICAL_SOURCES_PRE_V10/sources_recovered/NH_FINAL_MASTER_RECOVERY_STAGE_3A_CURRENT_AUTHORITY_FEATURE_BASELINE_v1.md` §7 **HISTORICAL SOURCES TO EXAMINE IN STAGE 3B** says: “These are NOT examined here. Stage 3B must walk the Stage 2 v1.1 §6 corrected queue and check each against this current baseline for any feature that was once present and is now weakened, dropped, or superseded”. It lists Masters 5–19, old Defaults, design addenda, and the pre-spine standalones.
- `98_HISTORICAL_SOURCES_PRE_V10/sources_recovered/NH_FINAL_MASTER_RECOVERY_FINAL_MATERIAL_NO_LOSS_CHECK_v1.md` §5 **Recovery closure** ends: “No further recovery stage is required.”

The evidence supports a gap between the Stage3B/final closure language and the explicitly recorded scope of the earlier comparisons. It does not establish what was done in any unseen conversation or file, and it does not judge adoption intent.

## Plain-language summary for Ness

These are ten consequential missing or changed items, selected for their effect on how the planned system would work. They are findings about the documents, not requests to bring old designs back. V10 and the settled decisions remain in charge.

1. **Image-tool guidance.** The old plan said to identify objects and their outlines before interpreting an image, and named tools for doing it. The current image section keeps the broad steps but no longer contains that choice or those names. See FR-0009.

2. **Checks across research results.** The old research plan required a fact to appear in at least two of three sets of search results. That particular check is missing from current governance. See FR-0081.

3. **Separate projects inside N.H.** The archive names separate, isolated project spaces inside N.H. No matching current requirement was found. This is different from the separate workspaces used to develop the project. See FR-0080.

4. **Detecting gaps in audit records.** The old hardening list required linked audit entries and detection of missing entries. Current logging remains, but this particular check was not found. See FR-0063.

5. **Recreating a working setup.** The old hardening list included a fixed dependency list, an exported environment, and compatibility tests before upgrades. Those specific requirements are missing from the current hardening entry. See FR-0064.

6. **What happens when the system is overloaded.** The old list called for queue and storage limits and an explicit account of what work waits under heavy load. The current documents do not retain that requirement. See FR-0065.

7. **Clinical reports and charts.** An old module list included clinical reports as PDFs and charts. Wellbeing features remain, but that specific output is not recorded in current governance. See FR-0082.

8. **Named speech tools.** The archive named Whisper for transcription and Piper/Coqui for spoken output, with noisereduce/librosa for cleanup. Current governance retains speech input and output but no longer names those candidates. This does not select any tool. See FR-0011, FR-0012, FR-0013, FR-0078, FR-0079.

9. **What one piece of meaning covers.** The old Meaning Engine sketch describes one piece as a whole sequence of changing states. V10 describes one piece as one state in that sequence. Those are different descriptions; this report does not choose between them. See FR-0103.

10. **Which context Engine B reads.** An early plan said Engine B would retrieve nearby material by meaning. V10 describes the built Engine B using preceding turns from the same conversation. The documents record a change in the source of its context. See FR-0096.

Separately, the audit recovered detailed bootstrap-reading and memory-health instructions beneath labels that current documents retain without their full bodies. Those are COMPRESSED findings, so they are not counted in the ten DROPPED/CONTRADICTED items above. Explicitly settled replacements—including the no-destruction law, sealed-cache inspection prohibition, and removed phone controls—are recorded as SUPERSEDED and are not reopened.
